about: Kogaki's settings for non-coding operation (kogaki#1307). Change a value here and the next run uses it; no code change and no Issue are needed. Every key below is required: a run that needs a key this file does not carry refuses, naming the key. Terrain's own values still live in src/terrain-workflow.json.

brief.call_limit_s_means: How long, in seconds, one call of a Brief job unit may run before it is stopped and asked again. A compose job unit makes two calls per Round (it composes one Candidate, then has its Move fit judged); a path-review unit makes one. A stopped call uses up one Round.
brief.unit_rounds_means: How many Rounds each Brief job unit gets, the first included. A Round is one answer handed to the validator or the Judge and the result on it. A refused answer or a stopped call uses one Round; an answer that is not readable at all is asked again without using one. There is no limit on the whole job. Its longest run is this number, times the calls per Round plus this number again (an unreadable answer is asked again up to this many times per Round, each a full call), times call_limit_s: with 3 Rounds, 2 calls and 900 s, a compose job unit can run 3 x 5 x 900 s, about 3 hours and 45 minutes, though a normal Round takes 10 to 15 minutes.
brief.compose_units_means: How many Candidates the compose job asks for at once, one job unit each.
brief.judge_model_means: The model every Brief judgment and every job unit is asked with.
brief.audience_file_means: The Audience file the Brief composes for. Its `persona` key says who the reader is and what they already know; its `register` key says how the prose addresses them.
brief.structure_readings_means: How many times the Brief reads the settled Strands into a structure before a Thesis is offered. Each reading is one job unit. The Thesis question offers the candidates that most readings agree on first and shows beside each how many readings produced it. With 1 the Brief reads once.
brief.thesis_words_means: The longest a Thesis may be, in words. A Thesis composed longer than this is rewritten once to fit before the Thesis question is shown, and the Brief stops, naming the length, if the rewrite is still too long. Words are counted between spaces.
brief.paragraphs_per_leg_means: The most paragraphs /paragraph-plan writes for one Leg of the Brief. The Leg's one bound Move shapes every one of its paragraphs, and a plan with more paragraphs under one Leg than this is refused, naming the Leg. Two is enough for a Leg whose Move first presents an analogue and then carries the inference back.

paragraph_plan.leg_revisions_means: How many Revisions one Leg of a /paragraph-plan job gets in total, across all of its paragraphs. A Revision is the next Submission at one paragraph, written to answer the Comment its last Submission drew, and it is written at that paragraph alone, under the Leg's bound Move. Each paragraph gets brief.unit_rounds Rounds, the Leg's first counting; this number ends a Leg whose Revisions keep reopening the paragraph after the one being repaired.
paragraph_plan.mapper_means: Whether /paragraph-plan runs the Mapper inside each Leg's job unit: it reads the Leg's relation into a structure before the Move is bound, grounds one Mapping Table for the bound Move after, and writes the Leg's Waypoints from that table. With false, the stage binds and writes the Waypoints in one call and the Mapping Record holds no file.
